reports.title: Jonathan Fry
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: There was no Senior review by a Consultant from admission to the time of his death and was no locum cover
There was no daily review of test results and no consideration given to instances where tests had not been performed or consoderation given to to the reasons why
concerns.hazard: lack of daily test result review

concerns.quote: Medical records were inconsistent and / or incomplete leading to a lack of clarity as to reviews and care plan

reports.title: Christopher Smith
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: A recommended home assessment was not completed as part of Mr [name redacted] planned discharge from hospital.
The next of kin was incorrectly recorded on Mr [name redacted] medical records and the family were not informed of his discharge home as part of the discharge planning that he required care.

Mr Smith remained on a discharge ward from 2nd February until his discharge on 10th February even though he suffered a deterioration in his medical condition. Mr [name redacted] capacity fluctuated during his admission, he was noted by nurses to be confused and his capacity was not reassessed.

Nursing notes in respect of Mr [name redacted] discharge were incomplete, incorrect, and led to assumptions being made that Mr Smith a. had capacity to make decisions about his care and treatment b. was being cared for in the community
Mr Smith has extensive leg ulcers that required specialist input. No district nurse referral was made to ensure that Mr [name redacted] leg ulcers were treated.

Transport staff returning Mr Smith home found he had no key. One was located and on entering the property found conditions that caused them serious concern about the hygiene and health and safety within the property with a leak, uncleanliness and exposed electrical wiring and that there was no bed.

reports.title: Kathryn Millard: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The Trust has also taken action to ensure that Anti-Embolic Stocking (AES) are prescribed and applied when indicated by the medical team. Safety messages and local teaching have occurred to ensure that nurses escalate incidents where an appliance has been indicated, but not prescribed. Since the recipient of this letter, the team has again sent out safety message to all nursing staff as a reminder of the expected standard. Compliance with expected practice will be audited monthly, and monitored
promises.summary: AES compliance audited monthly and taught to nurses

promises.quote: Changing the set up of the clinical team on the ward will allow the hierarchical tree with Change the 'Ward based structure to team based.
promises.summary: Transition to team-based structure to clarify responsibility

concerns.quote: The direction of the most senior clinician, the orthopaedic surgeon, was not documented in the medical records and was not implemented
concerns.hazard: lack of documented senior clinician direction

concerns.quote: The medical records indicated that at least one doctor had indicated that Mrs Millard should have anti-embolic stockings applied. However, the nursing staff gave evidence that they were not aware of this

The nursing staff were concerned on the 12 May 2021 as to the presentation and prognosis of the deceased. Whomever attended (if they anybody did in fact attend), did not make any entry into Mrs [name redacted] medical records

reports.title: Sally-Ann Few: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

promises.quote: The Trust Pharmacy team has contacted representatives of the Kent & Medway ICB Medicines Optimisation team that cover Medway & Swale. They are currently investigating the review process by the pharmacist to understand how the dose and product changes made were recorded and communicated to the GP practice. They are also investigating why these changes did not appear in the Kent Summary of Care Record.
promises.summary: Contact Kent & Medway ICB Medicines Optimisation team to investigate recording and communication of morphine dose changes to GP practice.

concerns.quote: Evidence given at the inquest revealed that the system at the GP practice when examined by the pharmacist at the hospital did not show that the Oromorph prescription had been stopped.
Evidence was heard that Mrs. Few whilst an in patient was prescribed Oromorph and not Zoromorph the drug she had been using at 20mg twice a day.

At the inquest it was clear that the standard of record keeping by the medical staff was poor and it was only by hearing from witnesses via statements and orally, including from her family, that the decision making around her care and plans for her management became clear, as there was very little written in the notes.
